title: Pochettino: USMNT’s Richards out vs. Germany with World Cup ‘decision’ looming
content:
CHICAGO — U.S. men’s national team center back Chris Richards finds himself in a World Cup race against time, after head coach Mauricio Pochettino admitted he will soon have to “make a decision” on the key defender’s tournament status.

Pochettino confirmed on Friday that Richards (ankle) will sit out the team’s World Cup send-off friendly against Germany at Soldier Field on Saturday. He missed last Sunday’s 3-2 win over Senegal, having previously remained on the bench for Crystal Palace’s UEFA Conference League final victory over Rayo Vallecano on May 27.

“He’s not ready to compete and to play,” Pochettino said. “In the next few days we have the possibility to assess him and his ankle, then to make a decision.”

Though Richards was named in the 26-man squad at U.S. Soccer’s squad unveiling event in New York on May 26 and official World Cup rosters were submitted to FIFA on June 1, teams can still make changes due to injury up until 24 hours before their first game. The USMNT faces Paraguay in Los Angeles on June 12, which puts Pochettino’s deadline on Richards at 9 p.m. ET on June 11.

Richards injured his ankle in a May 17 match for Crystal Palace. Friday marked his first time doing ball work with the full group during the portion of training open to media, after having previously spent that time training individually since his arrival at U.S. camp.

“Maybe if tomorrow was the final of the World Cup he could play, but the advice of the medical team was to not play,” Pochettino said.

Pochettino was not happy with the amount of information he had about the injury — whether from Palace or elsewhere — in order to make a decision on Richards’ status. The U.S. coach has come under some criticism for leaving players like Tanner Tessmann and Diego Luna off the roster, with both players having missed games due to injury before roster selection.

Pochettino indicated Friday that decisions were made more difficult based on the information he was given.

“When we decided on the squad list, we thought (Richards) could play in the UEFA Conference League final and that’s how we built the roster,” Pochettino said. “At the time, the information we had suggested that he might be able to play in that final against Rayo Vallecano. In fact, he was on the bench, among the substitutes. Then we thought he might perhaps be available against Senegal, as well. But in the end, the timelines kept getting pushed back, and that frustrates me a bit.

“I’m not happy about it, because we know he’s an important player, of course we all know that. But when I talk about the information we were working with, sometimes there isn’t much clarity in the end. We can keep waiting and hoping that Chris will be available, but as you said, we may end up with a player who arrives (at the World Cup) without having competed. Then we have to decide whether he’s fit enough to compete or not, and there isn’t much time during the World Cup.

“That’s why I say that, based on our thinking, we believed he was going to play in the Conference League final. … When I spoke earlier about a lack of information or about players not having played, what I meant was that perhaps the information we had wasn’t the information we should have been relying on to make the best decisions. We don’t want to find ourselves in a situation where we reach the second match and the player isn’t available.”

Richards is a central piece to the USMNT, the defensive anchor on the back line. If fit, he would be expected to play every minute for which he is available. Richards was called into six camps with Pochettino ahead of the World Cup roster being named and started 12 games, the fourth-most of any player in the pool under the Argentine manager.

The timing is brutal for Richards, who missed out on the 2022 World Cup due to injury. His teammates are looking forward to his potential return.

“Chris Richards is on the right path to coming back and being completely with the squad,” U.S. midfielder Weston McKennie said. “Everyone trusts his body, how he feels and the coaching staff. He’s an important piece to the group. His energy, leadership on and off the field, we’re all behind him and can’t wait to have him back.”
